title: Liquidation and lender shortfall in stressed Morpho markets
subtitle: Intraday replays, recovery rules and an on-chain event benchmark
author: Mohamed Rayan Bouchaibi
keywords: Morpho, lender shortfall, liquidation, pool depth, stress testing

ai_disclosure: Generative AI tools assisted in drafting and revising the manuscript and developing the replication code.
abstract: Across four historical crash paths on a captured WBTC/USDC borrower book, hourly liquidation checks reduce mean lender shortfall by 78 basis points of opening debt under a flat recovery haircut and 145 basis points when the remaining collateral of distressed loans is sold through a shared pool. Both results assume full daily refill. Loans that cover their debt at spot stay out of the closing sale. Direct quotes show that the pool approximation overstates proceeds for large sales. In a historical event replay of the same Morpho market, the engine identified 9 of 11 observed liquidated borrowers and reproduced 80% of on-chain repayment. Both the replay and the ledger showed zero realised bad debt.
